title: "Task 4(b): Multiclass webpage classification"
date: today
format: html
---

### Preprocessing

We modeled the cleaned paragraph text extracted from the labeled webpages. URLs, email addresses, punctuation, and digits were removed; text was lowercased and whitespace was normalized. A TF-IDF vectorizer represented each page using word unigrams and bigrams, with sublinear term-frequency scaling.

We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVM), and multinomial Naive Bayes using the same TF-IDF features. On a stratified 80/20 split (1,712 training pages and 428 validation pages; random seed 42), their validation accuracies were 78.5%, 81.3%, and 71.3%, respectively. We selected the linear SVM with class-balanced weights; the vectorizer used a minimum document frequency of one, and the SVM used its default regularization setting. The reported results are holdout estimates, not performance on the unlabeled prediction set.

### Results

The selected SVM correctly classified 348 of 428 validation pages (81.3% accuracy; macro-F1 73.8%). The table reports one-vs-rest sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for each class. The lower sensitivity for “Other claim content” and “Physical Activity” indicates that those categories were more difficult to identify; the former had only 20 validation examples.

| Class | Validation pages | Sensitivity | Specificity | One-vs-rest accuracy |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| N/A: No relevant content. | 203 | 82.3% | 82.7% | 82.5% |
| Other claim content | 20 | 40.0% | 97.3% | 94.6% |
| Physical Activity | 47 | 59.6% | 97.6% | 93.5% |
| Possible Fatality | 88 | 90.9% | 95.9% | 94.9% |
| Potentially unlawful activity | 70 | 92.9% | 98.0% | 97.2% |

Overall multiclass accuracy is the proportion of pages assigned the correct one of five labels. The class-specific measures treat each label as positive and all other labels as negative; therefore, one-vs-rest accuracy is distinct from overall multiclass accuracy.
